## claude.ai Crypto.com
Crypto.com Exchange MCP Server - Real-time cryptocurrency market data and interactive widgets.

- _OUTLOOK: Draft a fully-formatted email into Outlook for Mac — opens a ready-to-review compose window, never sends. Drives classic Outlook via AppleScript with HTML content so paragraphs, bullet lists, and numbered lists render correctly; degrades to a plain-text mailto draft if only New Outlook is present. Pulls recipient addresses from CONTACTS.md and writes in Nick's email voice. USE WHEN draft an email, write an email to X, email X about Y, open a draft in Outlook, compose an email, reply to X, send an email (draft it for review). NOT FOR actually transmitting mail unattended (this is draft-only), Gmail/web mail (no Outlook desktop), or bulk/broadcast sends (use _BROADCAST). Mac only — requires osascript.
- Agents: Compose CUSTOM agents from Base Traits + Voice + Specialization, and manage predefined functional TEAMS. Traits combine expertise (security, technical, research), personality (skeptical, analytical, enthusiastic), and approach (thorough, rapid, systematic). ComposeAgent.ts merges base + user config, outputs unique prompt + ElevenLabs voice + prosody. Predefined teams: engineering, architecture, marketing, design, security, research, content, strategy — each YAML-configured with roles, tensions, and specialist members. Observer team variant: read-only oversight agents that vote continue/halt/escalate against the tool-activity audit log (high-blast-radius or unattended runs only). USE WHEN create custom agents, spin up agents, specialized agents, agent personalities, available traits, list traits, agent voices, compose agent, spawn parallel agents, launch agents, engineering team, architecture team, marketing team, design team, security team, research team, content team, strategy team, get the team on this, observer team, audit agents. NOT FOR ad-hoc swarms or TeamCreate coordination (use Delegation). NOT FOR single-threaded delegation without unique identities (use Delegation Task).
- ApertureOscillation: 3-pass scope oscillation that holds a question constant while shifting the scope envelope — narrow/tactical, wide/strategic, then synthesis — to surface design tensions invisible at any single zoom level. Requires two distinct inputs: the tactical target (what you're building) and strategic context (the larger system it serves). Pass 1 captures the component's own internal logic. Pass 2 reveals what the system needs it to be. Pass 3 finds where those views diverge — that delta is the output. Produces: design tensions, scope recommendations, and coherence assessments. Single workflow: Workflows/Oscillate.md. BPE-fragile — quarterly test recommended to verify smarter models don't naturally oscillate scope without prompting. Best integration point: Algorithm OBSERVE phase (before ISC) or THINK phase (before approach commitment). NOT a lens rotation (that's IterativeDepth) and NOT idea generation (that's BeCreative). NOT FOR deep incident causal chains (use RootCauseAnalysis) or assumption decomposition (use FirstPrinciples). USE WHEN aperture oscillation, oscillate scope, zoom in and out, tactical vs strategic, scope framing, design tension, architecture decision, feature fits system, system coherence check, local vs global design, build this inside that, wrong scope, design review, scope negotiation.
- Aphorisms: Manages a curated aphorism collection with full CRUD — content-based matching, themed search, thinker research, and database maintenance. Organizes quotes by author, theme, context, and newsletter usage history to prevent repetition. Four workflows: FindAphorism (analyze newsletter content, match themes, return 3-5 ranked recommendations with rationale), AddAphorism (parse quote + author, extract themes, validate uniqueness, update theme index), ResearchThinker (deep research on philosopher, add sourced quotes to database), SearchAphorisms (search by theme, keyword, or author). Database at ~/.claude/skills/aphorisms/Database/aphorisms.md — stores full quote text, author attribution, theme tags, context/background, source reference, and usage history per entry. Theme index supports 12+ categories: Work Ethic, Resilience, Learning, Stoicism, Risk, Wisdom, Truth-seeking, Excellence, Curiosity, Freedom, Rationality, Clarity. Supported thinkers: Hitchens, Feynman, Deutsch, Sam Harris, Spinoza, plus any requested author. Newsletter integration: tracks which quotes used in which issues to enforce variety; content theme extraction drives automated matching. USE WHEN: aphorism, quote, saying, find a quote, research thinker, add aphorism, search aphorisms, quote for newsletter, what did X say about, quotes about [topic], quote bank, find matching quote, quote collection, add this quote, check usage history. NOT FOR general creative writing or social media post generation — those go through dedicated writing/social skill…
- Apify: Scrape social media platforms, business data, and e-commerce via Apify actors — Instagram profiles/posts/hashtags/comments, LinkedIn profiles/jobs/posts, TikTok profiles/hashtags/videos/comments, YouTube channels/search/comments, Facebook posts/groups/comments, Google Maps business search with contact/review/image extraction, Amazon products/reviews/pricing, and general-purpose multi-page web crawling with custom pageFunction extraction logic. File-based TypeScript wrappers (scrapeInstagramProfile, searchGoogleMaps, scrapeAmazonProduct, scrapeWebsite, etc.) filter and transform data in code before returning to model context, achieving 95-99% token savings over direct MCP protocol. Parallel multi-platform queries via Promise.all for social listening dashboards. Lead enrichment pipeline: Google Maps → qualified filter → optional LinkedIn enrichment. Competitive analysis across Instagram, YouTube, and TikTok simultaneously. USE WHEN scrape Instagram, scrape LinkedIn, scrape TikTok, scrape YouTube, scrape Facebook, Google Maps leads, Amazon reviews, business intelligence, multi-platform social listening, competitive analysis, lead generation, social monitoring, Apify actors, web crawl, extract contacts. NOT FOR X/Twitter bookmarks (use a dedicated X-API skill) or progressive scraping (use BrightData).
- Art: Generates static visual content across 20+ formats via Flux, Nano Banana Pro (Gemini 3 Pro), and GPT-Image-1. Covers blog header illustrations, editorial art, Mermaid flowcharts, technical architecture diagrams, D3.js dashboards, taxonomies, timelines, 2x2 framework matrices, comparisons, annotated screenshots, recipe cards, aphorism/quote cards, conceptual maps, stat cards, comic panels, YouTube thumbnails, PAI pack icons, and brand-logo wallpapers. Named workflows: Essay, D3Dashboards, Visualize, Mermaid, TechnicalDiagrams, Taxonomies, Timelines, Frameworks, Comparisons, AnnotatedScreenshots, RecipeCards, Aphorisms, Maps, Stats, Comics, YouTubeThumbnailChecklist, AdHocYouTubeThumbnail, CreatePAIPackIcon, LogoWallpaper, RemoveBackground. SKILLCUSTOMIZATIONS loads PREFERENCES.md, CharacterSpecs.md, and SceneConstruction.md. --remove-bg flag produces transparent-background PNG (can produce black backgrounds — verify visually). Up to 14 reference images per request (5 human, 6 object Gemini API limit). Output staged to ~/Downloads/ for preview before any project directory copy. Nano Banana Pro uses --size for resolution tier 1K/2K/4K and separate --aspect-ratio. USE WHEN: art, illustration, diagram, flowchart, infographic, header image, thumbnail, visualize, generate image, mermaid, architecture diagram, comic, icon, blog art, framework diagram, D3 chart, remove background, wallpaper. NOT FOR video or animation (use Remotion). NOT FOR the user's personal portrait/headshot (use a dedicated headshot skill).
- ArXiv: Search and retrieve arXiv academic papers by topic, category, or paper ID — with AlphaXiv-enriched AI-generated overviews. Uses arXiv Atom API (no auth) for discovery and search across cs.AI, cs.LG, cs.CL (NLP/LLMs), cs.CR (security), cs.MA (multi-agent), cs.SE, and cs.IR. Supports title (ti:), abstract (abs:), author (au:), and category (cat:) search fields with boolean operators (AND, OR, ANDNOT); sorts by lastUpdatedDate or relevance; paginates up to 2,000 results per call with 3s rate limit between calls. AlphaXiv enrichment fetches markdown summaries from alphaxiv.org/overview/{ID}.md; full text from alphaxiv.org/abs/{ID}.md as fallback; 404 means summary not yet generated. Workflows: Latest (new papers by category), Search (topic/keyword search), Paper (single paper deep-dive by ID or URL). API returns Atom XML — parse with text processing, not jq. HTTPS required with -L flag; check published date not lastUpdatedDate for truly new submissions. Output: paper title, authors, abstract, AlphaXiv summary, and direct arXiv URL. USE WHEN arxiv, papers, latest papers, research papers, new papers, what's new in AI research, recent ML papers, paper lookup, arxiv search, find paper by ID, summarize paper, latest NLP research, latest LLM papers, multi-agent papers, cs.AI latest, AI safety papers, software engineering papers, information retrieval papers. NOT FOR general web research (use Research), extracting content from arbitrary URLs (use Parser), or cybersecurity annual report analysis (use AnnualReports).
- AudioEditor: AI-powered audio and video editing pipeline: Whisper word-level transcription (insanely-fast-whisper on MPS) → Claude segment classification (KEEP / CUT_FILLER / CUT_FALSE_START / CUT_STUTTER / CUT_DEAD_AIR / CUT_EDIT_MARKER) → ffmpeg execution with 40ms qsin crossfades and room-tone gap fill → optional Cleanvoice API cloud polish for mouth sounds and loudness normalization. Distinguishes rhetorical pauses from accidental ones. Breaths attenuated to 50% volume (not removed). Preview mode (--preview flag) shows proposed cuts without modifying audio. Aggressive mode (--aggressive flag) applies tighter filler detection thresholds. Polish step (--polish flag) uploads to Cleanvoice API for mouth sound removal and loudness normalization — confirm before cloud upload of sensitive content. Pipeline tools: Transcribe.ts, Analyze.ts, Edit.ts, Polish.ts, Pipeline.ts. Single workflow: Clean.md. Requires ANTHROPIC_API_KEY; CLEANVOICE_API_KEY optional for polish step. USE WHEN: clean audio, edit audio, remove filler words, clean podcast, remove ums, cut dead air, polish audio, trim recording, audio cleanup, cut stutters, edit interview recording, preview edits, aggressive clean. NOT FOR video composition or animation (use Remotion).
- BeCreative: Divergent ideation and corpus expansion using Verbalized Sampling + extended thinking. Single-shot mode generates 5 internally diverse candidates (p<0.10 each) and surfaces the strongest. Multi-turn mode expands a small seed corpus (5-20 examples) into a diverse N-example dataset for evals, training, or test sets. Research-backed: Zhang et al. 2025 (arXiv:2510.01171) — 1.6-2.1x diversity increase on creative writing, 25.7% quality improvement, and synthetic-data downstream accuracy lift 30.6% → 37.5% on math benchmarks. Seven workflows: StandardCreativity, MaximumCreativity, IdeaGeneration, TreeOfThoughts, DomainSpecific, TechnicalCreativityGemini3 for algorithmic/architecture work, and SyntheticDataExpansion for VS-Multi corpus growth. Single-shot output is one best response, not a ranked list; SyntheticDataExpansion writes a JSONL corpus to MEMORY/WORK/{slug}/synthetic-data/. Integrates with XPost, LinkedInPost, Blogging (creative angles), Art (diverse image prompt ideas), Business (offer frameworks), Research (creative synthesis), Evals and _PROMPTINJECTION (consume expanded corpora). Reference files: ResearchFoundation.md (why it works, activation triggers), Principles.md (core philosophy), Templates.md (quick reference for all modes), Examples.md. NOT FOR multi-cycle evolutionary ideation with Lamarckian meta-learning (use Ideate for that). NOT FOR factually-constrained tasks with one right answer — paper §3.2 shows VS provides no lift there. USE WHEN be creative, think outside the box, brainstorm, diverg…
- BitterPillEngineering: Audits any AI instruction set for over-prompting using the core test: would a smarter model make this rule unnecessary? Applies Five Questions to every rule — Does Claude already do this? Contradiction? Redundant? One-off fix? Vague? — then classifies each as CUT / RESOLVE / MERGE / EVALUATE / SHARPEN / MOVE / KEEP. Two workflows: Audit (full system — reads all force-loaded files from settings.json, reports token savings estimate) and QuickCheck (single file, fast keep/cut/sharpen verdict). Outputs categorized report with estimated line and token savings. Core principle: less scaffolding = better output — every unnecessary rule competes for attention and degrades the rules that matter. Anti-fragile rules to KEEP: verification harnesses, ISC, data pipelines, specific DO/DON'T examples, tool preferences, routing rules. Fragile rules to CUT: CoT orchestrators, format parsers, retry cascades, numeric personality scales, abstract value statements. # Penny (envelope-os)

Zero-based envelope budgeting layer on top of PocketSmith, feeding PAI Pulse. AUD, single user, local-first, personal-finance-grade security.

- **Surface name:** Penny
- **Codebase folder:** envelope-os
- **System of record:** [`ISA.md`](./ISA.md) — twelve-section project ISA at E3 tier
- **Source thinking:** [`docs/REQUIREMENTS_CLARIFICATION.md`](./docs/REQUIREMENTS_CLARIFICATION.md), [`docs/ARCHITECT_REVIEW.md`](./docs/ARCHITECT_REVIEW.md)

## What it is

PocketSmith stays as the bank-feed and categorisation layer across ANZ, NAB, and Macquarie. Penny owns the envelope semantics that PocketSmith handles weakly. Allocation, spend-date cash basis, monthly and annualised budgets, rollover rules, time-travel views, and a read-only Pulse widget.

## Stack

bun plus TypeScript. SQLite via `bun:sqlite`. Hono API serving a Vite plus React plus shadcn SPA on one port. PocketSmith client codegenned from the pinned OpenAPI 3 spec. Tailscale-only access. No Python, no npm, no cloud storage of financial data.

## Status

ISA persisted, all design decisions locked (two architect-flagged contradictions resolved, see `ISA.md` Changelog). Build not started. Weekend 1 is the ingest spine. PocketSmith codegen client, SQLite schema, daily sync, two-year backfill.

content.text:
Yes — and that's exactly what the original ISA already bought you. "Tailscale-only access" doesn't mean home-wifi-only; Tailscale is a WireGuard mesh VPN, so your phone reaches the app over cellular from anywhere, as if it were on your home network.

**How it works locally + phone:**
- Tailscale on the host machine and on your phone — both join your private tailnet.
- `tailscale serve` gives the app a real HTTPS hostname on a `*.ts.net` domain. That matters: service workers (the PWA offline/install layer) require valid HTTPS, and this gives you a proper cert without exposing anything to the public internet. So you get a genuine installable PWA on your phone, fully private, ~$0.
- Financial data and your PocketSmith key never leave your own devices.

**The one real catch — an always-on host.** Your phone can only reach the app while the host is awake and running it. Both your machines are laptops (the XPS and the MacBook); a sleeping laptop = no access. If your Home Assistant setup runs on an always-on box (mini PC / Pi / NAS), Penny can ride on that same machine and you're sorted. If not, you'd want a cheap always-on host. That's the only thing local-first costs you.

**Here's the actual fork, and it's the one requirement that genuinely splits local vs cloud:**

Everything you listed — phone access, PWA, secure, your account, your transactions/budget/dev key — local-first delivers cleanly and near-free. The *only* thing it doesn't do well is **"give someone else access with just their email + their dev key."** On Tailscale, sharing means inviting their device onto your private network (node sharing) — that's friction, and it means letting an outside machine into your tailnet. Multi-tenant "email = access" is the single thing that actually forces public cloud hosting and all its security weight (storing other people's bank-API keys, public auth surface, ~$9/mo minimum).

**My recommendation:** you framed sharing as conditional ("*if* I wanted to give someone access"). That's optionality, not a confirmed need. So I'd build local-first now — faster to ship, near-zero cost, maximum privacy, and it satisfies every hard requirement except multi-user. The data model and PocketSmith integration are identical either way, so adding a hosted multi-tenant mode later is additive, not a rewrite. Don't pay the cloud security tax until someone actually needs a login.

So the decision I need from you:

needs input: Is third-party sharing a real near-term need, or just optionality? If optionality → I keep the local-first ISA, add the Tailscale-Serve PWA + phone access, and confirm you have an always-on host (does your Home Assistant run 24/7 somewhere?). If sharing is real and soon → I commit to the GCP multi-tenant re-architecture. Which way?

14	# Penny (envelope-os) — Project ISA
15	
16	> Surface name **Penny**. Codebase folder `envelope-os`. Zero-based envelope budgeting layer on top of PocketSmith, feeding PAI Pulse. AUD, single user, personal-finance-grade security, local-first.
17	
18	## Problem
19	
20	PocketSmith owns Nick's bank feeds and categorisation across ANZ (primary), NAB (credit card), and Macquarie, but its envelope handling is weak and it does not implement zero-based envelope budgeting. Dave Ramsey's EveryDollar and similar apps do implement the methodology but cannot connect to Australian banks. The result is that Nick runs envelope budgeting in his head on top of PocketSmith, which does not scale, does not survive a credit-card statement cycle cleanly, and gives no trustworthy single number for "where am I against budget right now". There is no time-travel view of envelope balances at a past date, no enforced every-dollar-allocated discipline, and no surface that feeds the state into Pulse.
21	
22	## Vision
23	
24	Nick opens Pulse and sees one honest line. Unallocated dollars, the worst three overspends, and whether the credit-card holding balance still matches NAB. He opens Penny at the start of a month, clicks "apply last month", adjusts three envelopes, and every dollar of expected income has a name before the month begins. When a late transaction lands weeks later, the envelope it belongs to moves on the day it was spent, not when the statement closes, so the budget never lies about the past. The euphoric surprise is the holding-versus-NAB tripwire. A single number that, when it drifts, tells Nick something is wrong before he would otherwise have noticed, and that he could never have computed by hand.
25	
26	## Out of Scope
27	
28	The MVP does not split one category across multiple envelopes. Mapping stays many categories to one envelope. A dedicated sinking-fund target type is not built. Annual envelopes are treated as monthly target divided by twelve for the MVP. There is no PWA, no mobile quick-add of purchases, and no offline capture. There is no auto-allocation engine and no agent-proposed allocations. There is no reporting suite beyond what the grid and detail pages show, no PDF or CSV export, and no what-if replay queries against the event log. There is no multi-currency support. There is no joint-finance surface. The data model reserves an unused owner column for that future, but no joint behaviour is built. Direct bank-CSV reconciliation against PocketSmith feeds is a later trust layer, not MVP.
29	
30	## Principles
31	
32	- The envelope is the user-facing primitive. PocketSmith categories are inputs. Envelopes are how Nick thinks and decides.
33	- Cash-basis fidelity to the envelope metaphor. A swipe decrements the envelope on the day it happens, regardless of which card moved.
34	- Every dollar is conserved. A forgiven overspend is not free money. The deficit is always booked somewhere, never silently leaked.
35	- Local-first. Personal financial data does not leave Nick's machine without a deliberate, per-action choice.
36	- The event log is the source of truth and the audit log. Future-Nick can always ask why an envelope went negative on a given day and get an answer.
37	- The thing is the source of truth, not the task. This ISA at the project root is iterated continuously, not recreated per task.
38	
39	## Constraints
40	
41	- bun plus TypeScript only. No Python. No npm or npx. Australian English. AUD only. No em dashes in prose.
42	- Storage is SQLite via `bun:sqlite`, single file, single writer owned by one Bun process. Not Postgres.
43	- The PocketSmith client is generated from the published OpenAPI 3 spec at `github.com/pocketsmith/api`, pinned to a commit SHA in-repo. The client is regenerated manually on a spec bump, never auto-tracked.
44	- Auth to PocketSmith is the `X-Developer-Key` header, key held in the PAI secrets store. Not OAuth. The key never appears in env files, git, or logs.
45	- Sync is daily pull only. PocketSmith publishes no webhooks, so no push or listener code path may exist. Incremental sync uses `updated_since`.
46	- Mobile and remote access is Tailscale-only. No public internet exposure.
47	- No cloud SaaS storage of financial data and no cloud AI inference over transactions by default. Opt-in is per query, never standing.
48	
49	## Goal
50	
51	Ship a local-first Penny that replaces Nick's PocketSmith-plus-mental-model setup with a real zero-based envelope view. Done means a daily PocketSmith pull lands transactions into a SQLite event-sourced ledger, envelopes decrement on spend-date with a visible Credit Card Holding envelope for NAB, a beginning-of-month wizard enforces every-dollar-allocated against expected income, the grid and a time-travel view render envelope balances, and a read-only Pulse widget surfaces unallocated dollars, top overspends, and the holding-versus-NAB tripwire. The four weekend phases each ship a coherent slice, and the holding-versus-NAB invariant is correct enough that its drift is trustworthy.

# Penny (envelope-os) — Project ISA

> Surface name **Penny**. Codebase folder `envelope-os`. Zero-based envelope budgeting layer on top of PocketSmith, feeding PAI Pulse. AUD, single user, personal-finance-grade security, local-first.

## Problem

PocketSmith owns Nick's bank feeds and categorisation across ANZ (primary), NAB (credit card), and Macquarie, but its envelope handling is weak and it does not implement zero-based envelope budgeting. Dave Ramsey's EveryDollar and similar apps do implement the methodology but cannot connect to Australian banks. The result is that Nick runs envelope budgeting in his head on top of PocketSmith, which does not scale, does not survive a credit-card statement cycle cleanly, and gives no trustworthy single number for "where am I against budget right now". There is no time-travel view of envelope balances at a past date, no enforced every-dollar-allocated discipline, and no surface that feeds the state into Pulse.

## Vision

Nick opens Pulse and sees one honest line. Unallocated dollars, the worst three overspends, and whether the credit-card holding balance still matches NAB. He opens Penny at the start of a month, clicks "apply last month", adjusts three envelopes, and every dollar of expected income has a name before the month begins. When a late transaction lands weeks later, the envelope it belongs to moves on the day it was spent, not when the statement closes, so the budget never lies about the past. The euphoric surprise is the holding-versus-NAB tripwire. A single number that, when it drifts, tells Nick something is wrong before he would otherwise have noticed, and that he could never have computed by hand.

## Out of Scope

The MVP does not split one category across multiple envelopes. Mapping stays many categories to one envelope. A dedicated sinking-fund target type is not built. Annual envelopes are treated as monthly target divided by twelve for the MVP. There is no PWA, no mobile quick-add of purchases, and no offline capture. There is no auto-allocation engine and no agent-proposed allocations. There is no reporting suite beyond what the grid and detail pages show, no PDF or CSV export, and no what-if replay queries against the event log. There is no multi-currency support. There is no joint-finance surface. The data model reserves an unused owner column for that future, but no joint behaviour is built. Direct bank-CSV reconciliation against PocketSmith feeds is a later trust layer, not MVP.

## Principles

- The envelope is the user-facing primitive. PocketSmith categories are inputs. Envelopes are how Nick thinks and decides.
- Cash-basis fidelity to the envelope metaphor. A swipe decrements the envelope on the day it happens, regardless of which card moved.
- Every dollar is conserved. A forgiven overspend is not free money. The deficit is always booked somewhere, never silently leaked.
- Local-first. Personal financial data does not leave Nick's machine without a deliberate, per-action choice.
- The event log is the source of truth and the audit log. Future-Nick can always ask why an envelope went negative on a given day and get an answer.
- The thing is the source of truth, not the task. This ISA at the project root is iterated continuously, not recreated per task.

## Constraints

- bun plus TypeScript only. No Python. No npm or npx. Australian English. AUD only. No em dashes in prose.
- Storage is SQLite via `bun:sqlite`, single file, single writer owned by one Bun process. Not Postgres.
- The PocketSmith client is generated from the published OpenAPI 3 spec at `github.com/pocketsmith/api`, pinned to a commit SHA in-repo. The client is regenerated manually on a spec bump, never auto-tracked.
- Auth to PocketSmith is the `X-Developer-Key` header, key held in the PAI secrets store. Not OAuth. The key never appears in env files, git, or logs.
- Sync is daily pull only. PocketSmith publishes no webhooks, so no push or listener code path may exist. Incremental sync uses `updated_since`.
- Mobile and remote access is Tailscale-only. No public internet exposure.
- No cloud SaaS storage of financial data and no cloud AI inference over transactions by default. Opt-in is per query, never standing.

## Goal

Ship a local-first Penny that replaces Nick's PocketSmith-plus-mental-model setup with a real zero-based envelope view. Done means a daily PocketSmith pull lands transactions into a SQLite event-sourced ledger, envelopes decrement on spend-date with a visible Credit Card Holding envelope for NAB, a beginning-of-month wizard enforces every-dollar-allocated against expected income, the grid and a time-travel view render envelope balances, and a read-only Pulse widget surfaces unallocated dollars, top overspends, and the holding-versus-NAB tripwire. The four weekend phases each ship a coherent slice, and the holding-versus-NAB invariant is correct enough that its drift is trustworthy.

## Criteria

### Ingest and sync (Weekend 1)

- [ ] ISC-1: PocketSmith TypeScript client generated from a pinned OpenAPI 3 commit SHA
- [ ] ISC-2: Client authenticates using the X-Developer-Key header
- [ ] ISC-3: Developer key resolved from the PAI secrets store at runtime
- [ ] ISC-4: Backfill pages through the transactions endpoint to completion
- [ ] ISC-5: Incremental sync passes updated_since equal to last successful run timestamp
- [ ] ISC-6: Backfill script pulls two years from a parameterised start date
- [ ] ISC-7: Daily sync runs from PAI cron at a fixed local time
- [ ] ISC-8: Two consecutive failed syncs raise a Pulse or Telegram alert
- [ ] ISC-9: Anti: No webhook listener or push-sync code path exists anywhere in the repo

### Data model and store (Weekend 1 to 2)

- [ ] ISC-10: SQLite database opens via bun:sqlite as a single file at a known path
- [ ] ISC-11: Schema declares events, snapshots, transactions, categories, mappings, envelopes tables
- [ ] ISC-12: Each transaction row stores the raw PocketSmith JSON for diffing
- [ ] ISC-13: transaction_overrides table is keyed on pocketsmith id and field
- [ ] ISC-14: An owner column exists on ledger entities, defaulted to the single principal
- [ ] ISC-15: Every state change appends an event with timestamp, actor, and correlation id
- [ ] ISC-16: End-of-day job writes one snapshot balance row per envelope per day
- [ ] ISC-17: Anti: Re-sync never mutates a transaction beyond base-field refresh plus overlay

### Envelope semantics (Weekend 2)

- [ ] ISC-18: Envelope CRUD persists name, group, rollover_rule, target_type, target_amount
- [ ] ISC-19: Category-to-envelope mapping is many-to-one and effective-dated
- [ ] ISC-20: Unmapped category transactions resolve to the Inbox envelope at import
- [ ] ISC-21: NAB card spend decrements the Credit Card Holding envelope on transaction date
- [ ] ISC-22: Transactions flagged is_transfer are excluded from envelope decrement
- [ ] ISC-23: Pending transactions appear in lists but do not decrement balances
- [ ] ISC-24: Posted transactions decrement the mapped envelope on transaction date
- [ ] ISC-25: Default rollover rolls positive and books a negative into next period available-to-allocate
- [ ] ISC-26: A roll_all override carries an envelope negative as visible debt
- [ ] ISC-27: Annual envelopes display as monthly target divided by twelve for the MVP
- [ ] ISC-28: Anti: A forgiven overspend never leaves the ledger unbalanced

### Allocation and every-dollar rule (Weekend 4)

- [ ] ISC-29: Beginning-of-month wizard offers apply-last-month as the default action
- [ ] ISC-30: Every-dollar rule is enforced at wizard completion against expected income
- [ ] ISC-31: Dashboard shows the expected-versus-actual income delta when they diverge
- [ ] ISC-32: Anti: Viewing the dashboard is never blocked by an unbalanced allocation

### UI (Weekend 3)

- [ ] ISC-33: Vite plus React plus shadcn SPA is served by Hono on a single port
- [ ] ISC-34: Envelope grid renders current-period balances in a Dave Ramsey layout
- [ ] ISC-35: Per-envelope detail page lists that envelope's transactions
- [ ] ISC-36: Time-travel date picker renders envelope balances as at end-of-day T
- [ ] ISC-37: Statement-period reconcile click confirms Holding matches NAB balance
- [ ] ISC-38: App is reachable only over Tailscale, not the public internet
- [ ] ISC-39: Session idle timeout is thirty minutes, unlocked by a secrets-store PIN

### Pulse (Weekend 4)

- [ ] ISC-40: Pulse job writes widget JSON to a known path on the daily cycle
- [ ] ISC-41: Pulse tile A shows unallocated dollars for the current period
- [ ] ISC-42: Pulse tile B shows the top three envelopes by overspend percent
- [ ] ISC-43: Pulse tile C shows Holding balance against NAB statement balance
- [ ] ISC-44: Every Pulse tile carries an as-of timestamp

### Security and data lifecycle (cross-cutting)

- [ ] ISC-45: Anti: No financial data is sent to cloud SaaS or cloud AI by default
- [ ] ISC-46: A daily encrypted backup of the SQLite file runs via rclone crypt remote

1	# EnvelopeOS — Requirements Clarification
2	
3	> Pre-build clarification doc. Staff-solutions-architect lens. No code yet. Goal: surface every meaningful design decision before the ISA is written.
4	
5	## 1. Summary of understanding
6	
7	Nick wants a zero-based envelope budgeting layer on top of his existing PocketSmith setup, because Dave Ramsey's apps do not connect to Australian banks and PocketSmith's envelope handling is weak. PocketSmith stays as the bank-feed and categorisation layer (ANZ primary account, NAB credit card, Macquarie account); a new app owns the envelope semantics (allocation, cash basis, monthly and annualised budgets prorated to month, time-travel views of envelope balances at any past date). UI must work on web and mobile. Sync from PocketSmith is undecided between API, periodic CSV export/import, and PAI Interceptor scraping. The envelope state should feed the PAI Pulse dashboard. This is personal financial data, so security is a first-class constraint.
8	
9	The trick of this project is that "zero-based envelope budgeting" is a specific methodology with specific edge cases (credit card spend, refunds, transfers between envelopes, mid-month income, annualised budgets, rollovers) and the build will live or die on whether the model matches Nick's mental model exactly. Most of the questions in section 6 exist to nail that down.
10	
11	## 2. Working name
12	
13	| Name | Pitch | Cost |
14	|------|-------|------|
15	| **EnvelopeOS** | Names the metaphor; "OS" signals it's part of the PAI surface. | Slightly heavy. |
16	| **Envelopes** | Single noun. Sits next to Pulse, Tasks. | Generic. |
17	| **Allocate** | Names the dominant verb — every dollar gets allocated in zero-based. | Less evocative; loses the cash-envelope image. |
18	| **Penny** | Compact, friendly, AU-acceptable; nod to Dave Ramsey's "every dollar has a name." | Could read as childish. |
19	
20	**Recommendation:** "Envelopes" for the codebase, "EnvelopeOS" as the long form when needed. Decide later. Penny is a tempting brand for a UI surface.
21	
22	## 3. Key assumptions
23	
24	1. **Single-user.** Nick's finances only. No joint surface in v1.
25	2. **AUD only.** No multi-currency in v1.
26	3. **PocketSmith is the bank-feed layer for the foreseeable future.** No direct bank integrations.
27	4. **Cash basis means: an envelope balance changes when the transaction date hits the ledger, not when the credit card statement clears.** Verify in question section.
28	5. **The envelope is the user-facing primitive.** PocketSmith categories are inputs; envelopes are how Nick thinks and decides.
29	6. **PocketSmith categories are stable enough to map.** If Nick reorganises categories monthly, the mapping layer becomes a real burden.
30	7. **Local-first canonical store.** Personal finance does not leave Nick's machine without a deliberate choice. Hosted SaaS is not on the table.
31	8. **Stack defaults.** bun + TypeScript, Postgres (this one genuinely warrants relational), Hono API, Next.js + shadcn/ui, PWA for mobile.
32	9. **Pulse widget is read-only.** Pulse surfaces "where am I against budget?" — it does not allocate or move money.
33	10. **Refresh cadence is daily.** Hourly sync from PocketSmith is overkill for the use case; daily is enough and simpler.
34	11. **Transactions imported are immutable.** Edits stay in Envelopes' overlay (e.g. envelope override) rather than mutating the source.
35	
36	## 4. Mental model of envelope budgeting (state this back so any mismatch surfaces now)
37	
38	**Zero-based budgeting means: every dollar of expected income for the period is allocated to a named envelope before the period begins; the sum of envelope allocations equals income; "unallocated" is itself an envelope that must be explicitly drained to zero.**
39	
40	**Envelope budgeting means: spending is tracked against the envelope, not against the account. An envelope is the budget — the bank account just holds the money on its behalf.**
41	
42	### Combined for Nick's case
43	
44	1. At the start of each month (or "budget period"), Nick decides where every expected dollar goes. Sum(envelope_allocations_this_period) = expected_income_this_period.
45	2. Envelopes have a starting balance for the period (rollover from prior period + allocation - any pre-period commitments).
46	3. Each transaction in PocketSmith carries a category. The category maps to one envelope. Hierarchy collapses: subcategories may have the same parent envelope; parent and child can also feed the same envelope.
47	4. Spend on a category decrements the envelope. Income to a category may either increase income-available-to-allocate (typical) or directly increase an envelope (rare — refund of a previous spend).
48	5. An envelope can be:
49	   - **Monthly target:** $X per month, resets each period.
50	   - **Annual target:** $Y per year, displayed pro rata against month (= Y/12) and against year-to-date (= Y * (months_elapsed/12)).
51	6. Rollover policy: each envelope has a rule. Options include: **roll positive, zero negative** (forgive overspend at period end), **roll all** (carry overspend as debt to next period), **drain to zero** (use it or lose it, e.g. monthly entertainment), **annual-only-resets-Jan** (most annual envelopes).
52	7. Time-travel: pick any past date `T`; show envelope balances as they were at end-of-day `T`. This requires storing every state change as an event, or storing daily snapshots, or computing on demand from the event log.
53	
54	### Credit card edge case (NAB) — the load-bearing question
55	
56	Three coherent ways to treat credit-card spend:
57	
58	| Model | When does the envelope decrement? | Where does the cash live? |
59	|-------|-----------------------------------|---------------------------|
60	| **A. Spend-date model** | When the card is swiped (transaction date). | A "Credit Card Holding" envelope accrues; when the card statement is paid, holding clears. |
61	| **B. Statement-date model** | When the statement closes. | Cash is in a normal envelope until statement close. |
62	| **C. Payment-date model** | When the card is paid. | Cash is in a normal envelope until payment hits. |
63	
64	Dave Ramsey purists use A. YNAB uses a variant of A. PocketSmith defaults to closer to spend-date. **Recommendation: model A — spend-date with a Credit Card Holding envelope.** Question 6.2 confirms with Nick.
65	
66	### Annualised envelope reconciliation
67	
68	If the car-registration envelope has a $900/year target, monthly display is $75. Year-to-date by end of June: $450 should have been accumulated. If Nick only allocated $50/month so far, he is $150 behind year-to-date. UI must show both **month progress** and **year progress** clearly, with a "true-up" suggestion when reality drifts.
69	
70	## 5. Preliminary architecture sketch
71	
72	### 5.1 Components
73	
74	```
75	+-----------------+    +------------------+   +-----------------+
76	|  PocketSmith    |--->|  Sync Worker     |-->|  Postgres       |
77	|  (bank feeds)   |    |  (bun cron)      |   |  (ledger,       |
78	+-----------------+    +------------------+   |   envelopes,    |
79	                                              |   snapshots)    |
80	                                              +---------+-------+
81	                                                        |
82	                                                        v
83	                                              +------------------+
84	                                              |  Hono API        |
85	                                              +---------+--------+
86	                                                        |
87	                                  +---------------------+----------+
88	                                  v                                v
89	                          +---------------+              +----------------+
90	                          |  Next.js web  |              |  PWA / mobile  |
91	                          +---------------+              +----------------+
92	                                  |                                |
93	                                  +---------------+----------------+
94	                                                  v
95	                                            +-----------+
96	                                            |  Pulse    |
97	                                            |  widget   |
98	                                            +-----------+
99	```
100	
101	### 5.2 Data model (first cut)
102	
103	```
104	Transaction
105	  id              text (PocketSmith id)
106	  date            date
107	  amount          decimal (signed; positive = inflow, negative = outflow)
108	  account_id      text (PocketSmith account)
109	  category_id     text (PocketSmith category at time of import)
110	  envelope_id     ulid (resolved through mapping table at time of import)
111	  payee           text
112	  note            text
113	  is_transfer     bool
114	  imported_at     timestamp
115	  raw_json        jsonb (PocketSmith payload, for diffs)
116	
117	Category
118	  id              text (PocketSmith id)
119	  name            text
120	  parent_id       text (nullable)
121	
122	CategoryMapping
123	  category_id     text
124	  envelope_id     ulid
125	  effective_from  date
126	  effective_to    date (nullable)
127	
128	Envelope
129	  id              ulid
130	  name            text
131	  group           text (Bills, Lifestyle, Savings, Annual, Sinking, etc.)
132	  rollover_rule   enum (roll_positive_zero_negative, roll_all, drain_to_zero, annual_reset_jan)
133	  target_type     enum (monthly, annual, sinking, no_target)
134	  target_amount   decimal
135	  active_from     date
136	  archived_at     date (nullable)
137	  display_order   int
138	
139	Allocation
140	  envelope_id     ulid
141	  period_start    date
142	  period_end      date
143	  amount          decimal
144	  source          enum (manual, recurring_rule, agent_proposed)

146	
147	Snapshot

153	
154	### 5.3 Time-travel implementation
155	
156	Three credible patterns:
157	
158	| Pattern | Detail | Pros | Cons |
159	|---------|--------|------|------|
160	| **Event-sourced ledger** | Every allocation and transaction is an event; balance at T = fold of events ≤ T. | Lossless, audit-friendly, supports "what if I had remapped X 6 months ago?". | Implementation complexity higher; queries need careful indexing. |
161	| **Daily snapshots** | One row per envelope per day with end-of-day balance. | Trivial queries. | 10 envelopes x 365 days = 3,650 rows/year — fine. Recompute on backfill is heavy. |
162	| **SQL with effective dates on every entity** | Each row carries effective_from/to. Balance computed at query time. | No background snapshot job. | Query complexity creeps; mapping changes get knotty. |
163	
164	**Recommendation: Event-sourced ledger + materialised daily snapshots.** The events table is the truth; the snapshots table is a cache rebuilt from the events. Time-travel queries hit snapshots; what-if queries replay events.
165	
166	### 5.4 PocketSmith integration — three paths
167	
168	Verified against PocketSmith's documented developer surface on 2026-06-11.
169	
170	| Path | What it is | Reliability | Effort | Risks |
171	|------|------------|-------------|--------|-------|
172	| **A. PocketSmith Developer API** | REST v2 at `https://api.pocketsmith.com/v2`. **Auth: `X-Developer-Key` header (single-user) or OAuth 2 (multi-user apps).** Endpoints cover transactions, categories, accounts, institutions, attachments, budget, events (forecast calendar, not webhooks), labels, currencies, users. **No plan-tier gate** — "the API is available for anyone to use without restriction and free of charge." Personal-use developer keys are generated in `Settings > Security` with no email registration. Transactions endpoint supports `updated_since` for incremental sync. OpenAPI 3 spec published at `github.com/pocketsmith/api`. **No webhooks.** | High — official, documented, OpenAPI-specced. | Low — codegen the client from OpenAPI, single-header auth, no OAuth dance. | Spec drift if PocketSmith refactors. Pin to commit SHA. Rate limits exist but are not aggressive at personal scale. |
173	| **B. CSV export/import** | Periodic manual export from PocketSmith UI, ingested into Envelopes. | Medium — depends on Nick remembering to export. | Lowest dev effort; highest user effort. | Stale data; copy-paste friction; reconciliation pain. |
174	| **C. Interceptor-driven scrape** | PAI Interceptor drives logged-in PocketSmith session, scrapes transactions list. | Medium — UI changes break it. | High dev effort and ongoing maintenance. | Could violate ToS; fragile; rate-limit risk. |
175	
176	**Recommendation: A as primary (developer key, codegen from OpenAPI), B as initial backfill and disaster-recovery fallback only. Drop C entirely.** The prior version of this doc hedged that API access might require Foundation plan; that hedge was wrong. There is no plan gate. Use OAuth 2 only if a multi-user surface is ever built. **No webhook support means daily pull is the only option — that's a feature, not a constraint, given the use case.**
177	
178	### 5.5 Security model
179	
180	- **Local-only by default.** API binds to localhost or Tailscale.
181	- **Postgres on the laptop.** No hosted DB. Daily encrypted backup to OneDrive (rclone with crypt remote, since the regular OneDrive cache has the 12h staleness issue your existing memory flags).
182	- **PocketSmith credentials in PAI secrets store.** Never in env files, never in git.
183	- **No cloud-side AI inference on transactions** unless Nick deliberately opts in per query.
184	- **Mobile access via Tailscale**, not public internet.
185	
186	### 5.6 Pulse widget
187	
188	Read-only tile showing: total income allocated this month, % allocated vs expected, top 3 envelopes by overspend, "you have $X unallocated" alert if income is in but allocation hasn't happened. Click-through opens the web app.
189	
190	## 6. Critical clarifying questions, grouped and prioritised
191	
192	### 6.1 Envelope semantics (highest priority — the model lives or dies here)
193	
194	1. **Confirm "every dollar allocated"** is a hard rule, not aspirational. Should the UI block save when income > sum(allocations)?
195	2. **Period boundary.** Monthly aligned to calendar month, to a pay cycle, or to something else?
196	3. **Initial allocation per month — manual every month, or carry forward last month's allocation as default?**
197	4. **Allocation pools.** Is there one income pool that gets allocated, or do allocations come directly from specific accounts?
198	
199	### 6.2 Credit-card treatment (the single most important question)
200	
201	5. **Which model — A (spend-date), B (statement-date), C (payment-date)?** *Recommendation: A.*
202	6. **Should the Credit Card Holding envelope be visible to Nick, or hidden plumbing?**
203	7. **What if Nick puts a purchase on NAB but funds were going to come from a different envelope conceptually — manual override per transaction, or a rule by category?**
204	8. **Card payment transactions from ANZ to NAB — automatically treated as transfers and excluded from envelope decrement, or visible?**
205	
206	### 6.3 Rollover rules
207	
208	9. **Default rollover rule?** Roll positive, zero negative is most popular; want this as default with per-envelope overrides?
209	10. **Negative envelope handling.** If an envelope ends the month at -$50, does the next month's allocation auto-cover it (true-up), or is the negative carried as visible debt?
210	11. **Annual envelope reset.** Always Jan 1, financial-year Jul 1 (AU), or per-envelope choice?
211	
212	### 6.4 Annual / sinking funds
213	
214	12. **Sinking-fund envelopes.** A category like "Holiday 2027" might have a target ($5,000 by Dec 2026) rather than monthly or annual. Need a sinking-fund target type?
215	13. **Display.** Show monthly proration with year-to-date, or just "track against absolute target"?
216	14. **What if Nick under-allocates an annual envelope for 4 months and wants to "catch up"?** Auto-suggest the catch-up amount?
217	
218	### 6.5 Category-to-envelope mapping
219	
220	15. **Mapping cardinality.** Many categories to one envelope is required. Do you also need one category split across multiple envelopes (e.g. "Groceries 80% Groceries envelope, 20% Household envelope")?
221	16. **Hierarchy.** If a parent category maps to envelope X and a child category maps to envelope Y, which wins for a transaction tagged with the child?
222	17. **Unmapped category handling.** Land in "Inbox" envelope until mapped, or block import?
223	18. **Mapping audit.** When PocketSmith renames or merges categories, what does Envelopes do?
224	
225	### 6.6 Transactions
226	
227	19. **Transaction edits in PocketSmith after import.** Re-sync wins, or local edit wins?
228	20. **Splits.** Some transactions need to split across two envelopes ($100 receipt = $60 groceries + $40 household). PocketSmith supports splits — do you mirror them, or split locally only?
229	21. **Transfers between Nick's own accounts.** Should they show in the ledger at all, or be filtered out entirely?
230	22. **Pending vs posted.** PocketSmith distinguishes pending and posted transactions. Show pending in envelope balances, or only posted?
231	
232	### 6.7 Time-travel
233	
234	23. **Granularity.** Day-level enough, or do you ever want intraday?
235	24. **What can you do at the past date — just view, or also "fix history" (e.g. remap a transaction that was wrongly categorised 4 months ago)?**
236	25. **If you change a category mapping today, does it apply retroactively or only forward?** Recommendation: choose at the mapping change time.
237	
238	### 6.8 PocketSmith sync
239	
240	26. ~~Confirm PocketSmith plan tier has API access~~ **Resolved 2026-06-11: no plan gate. Developer key on Free plan works.**
241	27. **Sync cadence.** Daily at a fixed time (e.g. 06:00) plus on-demand. (No webhooks available, so push is off the table.)
242	28. **Backfill window.** How far back should the initial sync pull? 2 years? Since-account-creation?
243	29. **Failure mode.** If sync fails for 2 days, alert via Pulse / Telegram?
244	
245	### 6.9 UI / UX
246	
247	30. **Primary surface — envelope grid (Dave Ramsey style) or list (YNAB style)?**
248	31. **Allocation ritual.** Beginning-of-month wizard, or "allocate as income arrives"?
249	32. **Bulk allocation shortcuts.** "Apply last month again with one click"?
250	33. **Spend entry on mobile** — read-only mobile, or quick-add purchases when offline (and reconcile later when PocketSmith catches up)?
251	34. **Notification on overspend** — push, Pulse, email? Threshold?
252	35. **Dashboard "you have $X to allocate" prominence.**
253	
254	### 6.10 Pulse integration
255	
256	36. **Widget content priorities.** Pick the 3 most useful tiles. Candidates: today's unallocated dollars, top 3 envelopes by overspend, days into period, total spend vs total budget, sinking-fund progress.
257	37. **Refresh cadence on Pulse.** Pulled on dashboard load, or pushed?
258	
259	### 6.11 Security and storage
260	
261	38. **Postgres locally, or DuckDB / SQLite for simpler ops?** Postgres warranted by time-travel queries.
262	39. **Backups.** rclone crypt to OneDrive, or somewhere else?
263	40. **Mobile access path.** Tailscale-only, or public with auth?
264	41. **Threat model.** Worst-case: laptop stolen. What protects the data? Full-disk encryption + Postgres password is probably enough — confirm.
265	
266	### 6.12 Reporting
267	
268	42. **Monthly close report.** Auto-generated end-of-period summary, or on-demand only?
269	43. **Spend-by-payee, spend-by-envelope drill-down** — v1 or v2?
270	44. **Export to CSV / PDF** for tax purposes?
271	
272	### 6.13 Multi-currency / joint finances (forward-look)
273	
274	45. **AUD-only confirmed for v1?**
275	46. **Joint-finance surface ever needed?** If yes, model it now even if hidden.
276	
277	### 6.14 Data lifecycle
278	
279	47. **Retention.** Keep all transaction history indefinitely, or auto-archive past 7 years?
280	48. **Deletion.** Can a transaction be deleted from Envelopes? (Recommendation: no — only marked excluded.)
281	
282	### 6.15 Auth
283	
284	49. **Single-user auth model.** PIN + Tailscale device trust, full password, or PAI session?
285	50. **Session timeout?**
286	
287	## 7. Open trade-offs needing Nick's call
288	
289	| Decision | Option A | Option B | Cost of getting it wrong |
290	|----------|----------|----------|--------------------------|
291	| **Credit card model** | Spend-date + holding envelope | Payment-date | A: matches Dave Ramsey, harder to explain at first. B: simpler, breaks "every dollar allocated" between spend and payment. |
292	| **Sync source** | PocketSmith API | CSV import | A: ongoing dependency on a third-party API and plan tier. B: monthly friction tax forever. |
293	| **Time-travel** | Event-sourced + snapshots | SQL effective-dating | A: more code, more durable. B: simpler now, harder later. |
294	| **Period boundary** | Calendar month | Pay cycle | A: ubiquitous, simple. B: aligns with cashflow reality but unusual. |
295	| **Mobile capability** | Read-only mobile | Quick-add on mobile | A: simpler. B: more useful when spending in the wild. |
296	| **Storage** | Postgres local | SQLite local | A: time-travel queries cleaner. B: zero-ops. |
297	
298	## 8. Suggested MVP scope
299	
300	**Goal: replace Nick's current PocketSmith-plus-mental-model setup with a real envelope view, within 3 to 4 weekends.**
301	
302	In:
303	- PocketSmith API sync (transactions + categories + accounts), daily cron
304	- Postgres ledger + event log + daily snapshots
305	- Envelope CRUD + category-to-envelope mapping (many to one)
306	- Credit card holding envelope (model A)
307	- Monthly allocation UI ("apply last month + adjust")
308	- Web dashboard: envelope grid + per-envelope detail with month progress
309	- Annual envelope proration display
310	- Time-travel "as of date" view (read-only)
311	- Pulse widget: unallocated dollars + top 3 overspend envelopes
312	- Tailscale-only mobile access
313	
314	Out of MVP:
315	- Splits across multiple envelopes
316	- Sinking-fund target type (treat as annual for MVP, add proper type in v1.0)
317	- Quick-add purchase from mobile
318	- Auto-allocation rules / agent proposals
319	- Bulk transaction editing
320	- Export to PDF / CSV
321	- What-if queries against the event log
322	- Reporting suite beyond monthly close
323	
324	Cut line: **if API sync doesn't work end-to-end with real data within weekend 1, kill the API path and switch to CSV import for MVP.**
325	
326	## 9. Risks
327	
328	| Risk | Likelihood | Impact | Mitigation |
329	|------|------------|--------|------------|
330	| PocketSmith API plan-tier surprise | Medium | Slip | Confirm plan now; budget for upgrade or fallback. |
331	| Category restructure in PocketSmith breaks mappings | Medium | Data quality | Effective-dated mappings + alert on unmapped category. |
332	| Credit-card model mismatch with Nick's mental model | Medium | Constant re-explanation | Settle in section 6.2 before code. |
333	| Time-travel correctness bug under category remap | Medium | Trust collapse | Replay tests; explicit "retroactive remap" toggle. |
334	| Sensitive data accidentally synced to cloud | Low | Privacy breach | Local-only by default; crypt remote for backups. |
335	| Bank feed lag at month boundary | High | Apparent overspend | Pending-transaction toggle in UI; reconcile button. |
336	| PocketSmith ToS / pricing change | Low to medium | Architectural lock-in | Keep transaction model bank-agnostic; PocketSmith is a source, not the contract. |
337	| Pulse widget over-promises ("you're $X under") then a late transaction blows it | Medium | Confidence dip | Show "as of" timestamp prominently. |
338	
339	## 10. Recommended next step
340	
341	Nick answers the highest-priority questions in section 6 (specifically 1, 2, 5, 6, 9, 11, 15, 19, 26, 30, 31, 36, 40). With those answers locked, an architect agent writes the ISA against `~/.claude/PAI/DOCUMENTATION/IsaFormat.md`, and a feature-dev agent ships the API sync + Postgres ledger + envelope grid within weekend 1. Allocation UI and Pulse widget follow in weekend 2.

# EnvelopeOS — Requirements Clarification

> Pre-build clarification doc. Staff-solutions-architect lens. No code yet. Goal: surface every meaningful design decision before the ISA is written.

## 1. Summary of understanding

Nick wants a zero-based envelope budgeting layer on top of his existing PocketSmith setup, because Dave Ramsey's apps do not connect to Australian banks and PocketSmith's envelope handling is weak. PocketSmith stays as the bank-feed and categorisation layer (ANZ primary account, NAB credit card, Macquarie account); a new app owns the envelope semantics (allocation, cash basis, monthly and annualised budgets prorated to month, time-travel views of envelope balances at any past date). UI must work on web and mobile. Sync from PocketSmith is undecided between API, periodic CSV export/import, and PAI Interceptor scraping. The envelope state should feed the PAI Pulse dashboard. This is personal financial data, so security is a first-class constraint.

The trick of this project is that "zero-based envelope budgeting" is a specific methodology with specific edge cases (credit card spend, refunds, transfers between envelopes, mid-month income, annualised budgets, rollovers) and the build will live or die on whether the model matches Nick's mental model exactly. Most of the questions in section 6 exist to nail that down.

## 2. Working name

| Name | Pitch | Cost |
|------|-------|------|
| **EnvelopeOS** | Names the metaphor; "OS" signals it's part of the PAI surface. | Slightly heavy. |
| **Envelopes** | Single noun. Sits next to Pulse, Tasks. | Generic. |
| **Allocate** | Names the dominant verb — every dollar gets allocated in zero-based. | Less evocative; loses the cash-envelope image. |
| **Penny** | Compact, friendly, AU-acceptable; nod to Dave Ramsey's "every dollar has a name." | Could read as childish. |

**Recommendation:** "Envelopes" for the codebase, "EnvelopeOS" as the long form when needed. Decide later. Penny is a tempting brand for a UI surface.

## 3. Key assumptions

1. **Single-user.** Nick's finances only. No joint surface in v1.
2. **AUD only.** No multi-currency in v1.
3. **PocketSmith is the bank-feed layer for the foreseeable future.** No direct bank integrations.
4. **Cash basis means: an envelope balance changes when the transaction date hits the ledger, not when the credit card statement clears.** Verify in question section.
5. **The envelope is the user-facing primitive.** PocketSmith categories are inputs; envelopes are how Nick thinks and decides.
6. **PocketSmith categories are stable enough to map.** If Nick reorganises categories monthly, the mapping layer becomes a real burden.
7. **Local-first canonical store.** Personal finance does not leave Nick's machine without a deliberate choice. Hosted SaaS is not on the table.
8. **Stack defaults.** bun + TypeScript, Postgres (this one genuinely warrants relational), Hono API, Next.js + shadcn/ui, PWA for mobile.
9. **Pulse widget is read-only.** Pulse surfaces "where am I against budget?" — it does not allocate or move money.
10. **Refresh cadence is daily.** Hourly sync from PocketSmith is overkill for the use case; daily is enough and simpler.
11. **Transactions imported are immutable.** Edits stay in Envelopes' overlay (e.g. envelope override) rather than mutating the source.

## 4. Mental model of envelope budgeting (state this back so any mismatch surfaces now)

**Zero-based budgeting means: every dollar of expected income for the period is allocated to a named envelope before the period begins; the sum of envelope allocations equals income; "unallocated" is itself an envelope that must be explicitly drained to zero.**

**Envelope budgeting means: spending is tracked against the envelope, not against the account. An envelope is the budget — the bank account just holds the money on its behalf.**

### Combined for Nick's case

1. At the start of each month (or "budget period"), Nick decides where every expected dollar goes. Sum(envelope_allocations_this_period) = expected_income_this_period.
2. Envelopes have a starting balance for the period (rollover from prior period + allocation - any pre-period commitments).
3. Each transaction in PocketSmith carries a category. The category maps to one envelope. Hierarchy collapses: subcategories may have the same parent envelope; parent and child can also feed the same envelope.
4. Spend on a category decrements the envelope. Income to a category may either increase income-available-to-allocate (typical) or directly increase an envelope (rare — refund of a previous spend).
5. An envelope can be:
   - **Monthly target:** $X per month, resets each period.
   - **Annual target:** $Y per year, displayed pro rata against month (= Y/12) and against year-to-date (= Y * (months_elapsed/12)).
6. Rollover policy: each envelope has a rule. Options include: **roll positive, zero negative** (forgive overspend at period end), **roll all** (carry overspend as debt to next period), **drain to zero** (use it or lose it, e.g. monthly entertainment), **annual-only-resets-Jan** (most annual envelopes).
7. Time-travel: pick any past date `T`; show envelope balances as they were at end-of-day `T`. This requires storing every state change as an event, or storing daily snapshots, or computing on demand from the event log.

### Credit card edge case (NAB) — the load-bearing question

Three coherent ways to treat credit-card spend:

| Model | When does the envelope decrement? | Where does the cash live? |
|-------|-----------------------------------|---------------------------|
| **A. Spend-date model** | When the card is swiped (transaction date). | A "Credit Card Holding" envelope accrues; when the card statement is paid, holding clears. |
| **B. Statement-date model** | When the statement closes. | Cash is in a normal envelope until statement close. |
| **C. Payment-date model** | When the card is paid. | Cash is in a normal envelope until payment hits. |

Dave Ramsey purists use A. YNAB uses a variant of A. PocketSmith defaults to closer to spend-date. **Recommendation: model A — spend-date with a Credit Card Holding envelope.** Question 6.2 confirms with Nick.

### Annualised envelope reconciliation

If the car-registration envelope has a $900/year target, monthly display is $75. Year-to-date by end of June: $450 should have been accumulated. If Nick only allocated $50/month so far, he is $150 behind year-to-date. UI must show both **month progress** and **year progress** clearly, with a "true-up" suggestion when reality drifts.

## 5. Preliminary architecture sketch

### 5.1 Components

                                                        |

                                                        |

                                  v                                v
                          +---------------+              +----------------+
                          |  Next.js web  |              |  PWA / mobile  |

                                  |                                |
                                  +---------------+----------------+
                                                  v

                                            +-----------+
```

  rollover_rule   enum (roll_positive_zero_negative, roll_all, drain_to_zero, annual_reset_jan)
  target_type     enum (monthly, annual, sinking, no_target)
  target_amount   decimal
  active_from     date
  archived_at     date (nullable)
  display_order   int

Allocation

  period_start    date
  period_end      date

  envelope_id     ulid
  balance         decimal
  computed_at     timestamp
```

### 5.3 Time-travel implementation

Three credible patterns:

| Pattern | Detail | Pros | Cons |
|---------|--------|------|------|
| **Event-sourced ledger** | Every allocation and transaction is an event; balance at T = fold of events ≤ T. | Lossless, audit-friendly, supports "what if I had remapped X 6 months ago?". | Implementation complexity higher; queries need careful indexing. |
| **Daily snapshots** | One row per envelope per day with end-of-day balance. | Trivial queries. | 10 envelopes x 365 days = 3,650 rows/year — fine. Recompute on backfill is heavy. |
| **SQL with effective dates on every entity** | Each row carries effective_from/to. Balance computed at query time. | No background snapshot job. | Query complexity creeps; mapping changes get knotty. |

**Recommendation: Event-sourced ledger + materialised daily snapshots.** The events table is the truth; the snapshots table is a cache rebuilt from the events. Time-travel queries hit snapshots; what-if queries replay events.

### 5.4 PocketSmith integration — three paths

Verified against PocketSmith's documented developer surface on 2026-06-11.

| Path | What it is | Reliability | Effort | Risks |
|------|------------|-------------|--------|-------|
| **A. PocketSmith Developer API** | REST v2 at `https://api.pocketsmith.com/v2`. **Auth: `X-Developer-Key` header (single-user) or OAuth 2 (multi-user apps).** Endpoints cover transactions, categories, accounts, institutions, attachments, budget, events (forecast calendar, not webhooks), labels, currencies, users. **No plan-tier gate** — "the API is available for anyone to use without restriction and free of charge." Personal-use developer keys are generated in `Settings > Security` with no email registration. Transactions endpoint supports `updated_since` for incremental sync. OpenAPI 3 spec published at `github.com/pocketsmith/api`. **No webhooks.** | High — official, documented, OpenAPI-specced. | Low — codegen the client from OpenAPI, single-header auth, no OAuth dance. | Spec drift if PocketSmith refactors. Pin to commit SHA. Rate limits exist but are not aggressive at personal scale. |
| **B. CSV export/import** | Periodic manual export from PocketSmith UI, ingested into Envelopes. | Medium — depends on Nick remembering to export. | Lowest dev effort; highest user effort. | Stale data; copy-paste friction; reconciliation pain. |
| **C. Interceptor-driven scrape** | PAI Interceptor drives logged-in PocketSmith session, scrapes transactions list. | Medium — UI changes break it. | High dev effort and ongoing maintenance. | Could violate ToS; fragile; rate-limit risk. |

**Recommendation: A as primary (developer key, codegen from OpenAPI), B as initial backfill and disaster-recovery fallback only. Drop C entirely.** The prior version of this doc hedged that API access might require Foundation plan; that hedge was wrong. There is no plan gate. Use OAuth 2 only if a multi-user surface is ever built. **No webhook support means daily pull is the only option — that's a feature, not a constraint, given the use case.**

### 5.5 Security model

- **Local-only by default.** API binds to localhost or Tailscale.
- **Postgres on the laptop.** No hosted DB. Daily encrypted backup to OneDrive (rclone with crypt remote, since the regular OneDrive cache has the 12h staleness issue your existing memory flags).
- **PocketSmith credentials in PAI secrets store.** Never in env files, never in git.
- **No cloud-side AI inference on transactions** unless Nick deliberately opts in per query.
- **Mobile access via Tailscale**, not public internet.

### 5.6 Pulse widget

Read-only tile showing: total income allocated this month, % allocated vs expected, top 3 envelopes by overspend, "you have $X unallocated" alert if income is in but allocation hasn't happened. Click-through opens the web app.

## 6. Critical clarifying questions, grouped and prioritised

### 6.1 Envelope semantics (highest priority — the model lives or dies here)

1. **Confirm "every dollar allocated"** is a hard rule, not aspirational. Should the UI block save when income > sum(allocations)?
2. **Period boundary.** Monthly aligned to calendar month, to a pay cycle, or to something else?
3. **Initial allocation per month — manual every month, or carry forward last month's allocation as default?**
4. **Allocation pools.** Is there one income pool that gets allocated, or do allocations come directly from specific accounts?

### 6.2 Credit-card treatment (the single most important question)

5. **Which model — A (spend-date), B (statement-date), C (payment-date)?** *Recommendation: A.*
6. **Should the Credit Card Holding envelope be visible to Nick, or hidden plumbing?**
7. **What if Nick puts a purchase on NAB but funds were going to come from a different envelope conceptually — manual override per transaction, or a rule by category?**
8. **Card payment transactions from ANZ to NAB — automatically treated as transfers and excluded from envelope decrement, or visible?**

### 6.3 Rollover rules

9. **Default rollover rule?** Roll positive, zero negative is most popular; want this as default with per-envelope overrides?
10. **Negative envelope handling.** If an envelope ends the month at -$50, does the next month's allocation auto-cover it (true-up), or is the negative carried as visible debt?
11. **Annual envelope reset.** Always Jan 1, financial-year Jul 1 (AU), or per-envelope choice?

### 6.4 Annual / sinking funds

12. **Sinking-fund envelopes.** A category like "Holiday 2027" might have a target ($5,000 by Dec 2026) rather than monthly or annual. Need a sinking-fund target type?
13. **Display.** Show monthly proration with year-to-date, or just "track against absolute target"?
14. **What if Nick under-allocates an annual envelope for 4 months and wants to "catch up"?** Auto-suggest the catch-up amount?

### 6.5 Category-to-envelope mapping

15. **Mapping cardinality.** Many categories to one envelope is required. Do you also need one category split across multiple envelopes (e.g. "Groceries 80% Groceries envelope, 20% Household envelope")?
16. **Hierarchy.** If a parent category maps to envelope X and a child category maps to envelope Y, which wins for a transaction tagged with the child?
17. **Unmapped category handling.** Land in "Inbox" envelope until mapped, or block import?
18. **Mapping audit.** When PocketSmith renames or merges categories, what does Envelopes do?

### 6.6 Transactions

19. **Transaction edits in PocketSmith after import.** Re-sync wins, or local edit wins?
20. **Splits.** Some transactions need to split across two envelopes ($100 receipt = $60 groceries + $40 household). PocketSmith supports splits — do you mirror them, or split locally only?
21. **Transfers between Nick's own accounts.** Should they show in the ledger at all, or be filtered out entirely?
22. **Pending vs posted.** PocketSmith distinguishes pending and posted transactions. Show pending in envelope balances, or only posted?

### 6.7 Time-travel

23. **Granularity.** Day-level enough, or do you ever want intraday?
24. **What can you do at the past date — just view, or also "fix history" (e.g. remap a transaction that was wrongly categorised 4 months ago)?**
25. **If you change a category mapping today, does it apply retroactively or only forward?** Recommendation: choose at the mapping change time.

### 6.8 PocketSmith sync

26. ~~Confirm PocketSmith plan tier has API access~~ **Resolved 2026-06-11: no plan gate. Developer key on Free plan works.**
27. **Sync cadence.** Daily at a fixed time (e.g. 06:00) plus on-demand. (No webhooks available, so push is off the table.)
28. **Backfill window.** How far back should the initial sync pull? 2 years? Since-account-creation?
29. **Failure mode.** If sync fails for 2 days, alert via Pulse / Telegram?

### 6.9 UI / UX

30. **Primary surface — envelope grid (Dave Ramsey style) or list (YNAB style)?**
31. **Allocation ritual.** Beginning-of-month wizard, or "allocate as income arrives"?
32. **Bulk allocation shortcuts.** "Apply last month again with one click"?
33. **Spend entry on mobile** — read-only mobile, or quick-add purchases when offline (and reconcile later when PocketSmith catches up)?
34. **Notification on overspend** — push, Pulse, email? Threshold?
35. **Dashboard "you have $X to allocate" prominence.**

### 6.10 Pulse integration

36. **Widget content priorities.** Pick the 3 most useful tiles. Candidates: today's unallocated dollars, top 3 envelopes by overspend, days into period, total spend vs total budget, sinking-fund progress.
37. **Refresh cadence on Pulse.** Pulled on dashboard load, or pushed?

### 6.11 Security and storage

38. **Postgres locally, or DuckDB / SQLite for simpler ops?** Postgres warranted by time-travel queries.
39. **Backups.** rclone crypt to OneDrive, or somewhere else?
40. **Mobile access path.** Tailscale-only, or public with auth?
41. **Threat model.** Worst-case: laptop stolen. What protects the data? Full-disk encryption + Postgres password is probably enough — confirm.

### 6.12 Reporting

42. **Monthly close report.** Auto-generated end-of-period summary, or on-demand only?
43. **Spend-by-payee, spend-by-envelope drill-down** — v1 or v2?
44. **Export to CSV / PDF** for tax purposes?

### 6.13 Multi-currency / joint finances (forward-look)

45. **AUD-only confirmed for v1?**
46. **Joint-finance surface ever needed?** If yes, model it now even if hidden.

### 6.14 Data lifecycle

47. **Retention.** Keep all transaction history indefinitely, or auto-archive past 7 years?
48. **Deletion.** Can a transaction be deleted from Envelopes? (Recommendation: no — only marked excluded.)

### 6.15 Auth

49. **Single-user auth model.** PIN + Tailscale device trust, full password, or PAI session?
50. **Session timeout?**

## 7. Open trade-offs needing Nick's call

| Decision | Option A | Option B | Cost of getting it wrong |
|----------|----------|----------|--------------------------|
| **Credit card model** | Spend-date + holding envelope | Payment-date | A: matches Dave Ramsey, harder to explain at first. B: simpler, breaks "every dollar allocated" between spend and payment. |
| **Sync source** | PocketSmith API | CSV import | A: ongoing dependency on a third-party API and plan tier. B: monthly friction tax forever. |
| **Time-travel** | Event-sourced + snapshots | SQL effective-dating | A: more code, more durable. B: simpler now, harder later. |
| **Period boundary** | Calendar month | Pay cycle | A: ubiquitous, simple. B: aligns with cashflow reality but unusual. |
| **Mobile capability** | Read-only mobile | Quick-add on mobile | A: simpler. B: more useful when spending in the wild. |
| **Storage** | Postgres local | SQLite local | A: time-travel queries cleaner. B: zero-ops. |

## 8. Suggested MVP scope

**Goal: replace Nick's current PocketSmith-plus-mental-model setup with a real envelope view, within 3 to 4 weekends.**

In:
- PocketSmith API sync (transactions + categories + accounts), daily cron
- Postgres ledger + event log + daily snapshots
- Envelope CRUD + category-to-envelope mapping (many to one)
- Credit card holding envelope (model A)
- Monthly allocation UI ("apply last month + adjust")
- Web dashboard: envelope grid + per-envelope detail with month progress
- Annual envelope proration display
- Time-travel "as of date" view (read-only)
- Pulse widget: unallocated dollars + top 3 overspend envelopes
- Tailscale-only mobile access

Out of MVP:
- Splits across multiple envelopes
- Sinking-fund target type (treat as annual for MVP, add proper type in v1.0)
- Quick-add purchase from mobile
- Auto-allocation rules / agent proposals
- Bulk transaction editing
- Export to PDF / CSV
- What-if queries against the event log
- Reporting suite beyond monthly close

Cut line: **if API sync doesn't work end-to-end with real data within weekend 1, kill the API path and switch to CSV import for MVP.**

## 9. Risks

| Risk | Likelihood | Impact | Mitigation |
|------|------------|--------|------------|
| PocketSmith API plan-tier surprise | Medium | Slip | Confirm plan now; budget for upgrade or fallback. |
| Category restructure in PocketSmith breaks mappings | Medium | Data quality | Effective-dated mappings + alert on unmapped category. |
| Credit-card model mismatch with Nick's mental model | Medium | Constant re-explanation | Settle in section 6.2 before code. |
| Time-travel correctness bug under category remap | Medium | Trust collapse | Replay tests; explicit "retroactive remap" toggle. |
| Sensitive data accidentally synced to cloud | Low | Privacy breach | Local-only by default; crypt remote for backups. |
| Bank feed lag at month boundary | High | Apparent overspend | Pending-transaction toggle in UI; reconcile button. |
| PocketSmith ToS / pricing change | Low to medium | Architectural lock-in | Keep transaction model bank-agnostic; PocketSmith is a source, not the contract. |
| Pulse widget over-promises ("you're $X under") then a late transaction blows it | Medium | Confidence dip | Show "as of" timestamp prominently. |

## 10. Recommended next step

Nick answers the highest-priority questions in section 6 (specifically 1, 2, 5, 6, 9, 11, 15, 19, 26, 30, 31, 36, 40). With those answers locked, an architect agent writes the ISA against `~/.claude/PAI/DOCUMENTATION/IsaFormat.md`, and a feature-dev agent ships the API sync + Postgres ledger + envelope grid within weekend 1. Allocation UI and Pulse widget follow in weekend 2.
